reject_reason: other: invalid evidence; the repo's own code contradicts the claim (the C++ port's decoder is unimplemented and has no AVX-512 code), and the only numbers are search snippets about the separate Go/assembly implementation
tier_reason: The SnellerInc/iguana repo has a one-line README ('A C iguana compression port'), no benchmark code and no numbers. The 30-33% faster-than-LZ4 figure is known only from HN/encode.su search snippets and refers to Sneller's original Go+AVX-512 assembly implementation, not to this repo. In this repo, iguana/decoder.cpp's decoder::decompress starts with IGUANA_UNIMPLEMENTED, the ans1/ans32/ans_nibble decode branches are also IGUANA_UNIMPLEMENTED with the Go code left in /*TODO*/ comments, and no file checked (decoder.cpp, ans1.cpp, ans32.cpp, ans_nibble.cpp, platform.h) has any _mm512/AVX-512 intrinsics.

corrections.claimed_speedup: None for this repo. HN/encode.su search snippets (pages not opened) say Sneller's original Go+AVX-512 iguana decompresses about 30% faster than LZ4 with entropy coding off, and about 2x faster than zstd on Silesia with entropy coding on (Xeon Gold 5320, 2260 MB/s). That is a different implementation from this C++ port, which cannot decompress.
corrections.caveats: This is an unfinished C++ port: decoder::decompress and the ANS decode paths call IGUANA_UNIMPLEMENTED, with the Go source left in TODO comments, and there are no AVX-512 kernels. The SIMD claims belong to the Go/assembly original inside Sneller's codebase. ClickHouse PR #107560 (closed 2026-09-10) finished the port in a ClickHouse fork with SIMD decode and dispatch. On ClickBench it measured the same ratio as ZSTD(3) but 1.21x-2.37x slower hot queries, and on the URL column it decompressed at 429 MB/s against 1807 MB/s for ZSTD(3). The PR review found a decompression-bomb risk and a format limit that cannot round-trip matches longer than about 16.5 MiB. The author closed the PR because the codec did not justify inclusion. TurboBench calls the ClickHouse fork 'Not reliable'.

notes: Rejected for invalid evidence under the harness rule: the repo's own code contradicts the claim (the decoder is unimplemented and has no SIMD). If the orchestrator wants Iguana listed, the right target is the original Go+asm implementation in SnellerInc/sneller (its path was not found at ion/zion/iguana, iguana/ or compr/iguana) or the ClickHouse fork. Even then, ClickHouse PR #107560 measured it slower than ZSTD(3) on decompression. License Apache-2.0, 3 stars, 76 commits, last commit 2023-11-03, all confirmed.

tier_reason: The README's Benchmarks section gives a single first-party run against the standard zip utility on Matt Mahoney's 10GB sample directory: zip real 14m31.809s / user 13m12.833s, pzip real 0m56.851s / user 3m32.619s. It states no CPU model, core count, zip version or compression level, and has no benchmark script, so it is tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: zip: real 14m31.809s, user 13m12.833s, sys 0m24.193s; pzip: real 0m56.851s, user 3m32.619s, sys 1m25.040s. About 15.3x less wall time and about 3.7x less user CPU time (derived from page data).
corrections.baseline: standard zip utility (Info-ZIP zip, single-threaded DEFLATE)
corrections.caveats: The speedup comes mostly from per-file concurrency over a single-threaded baseline. pzip also uses klauspost/compress v1.16.7 (go.mod) instead of zlib-based DEFLATE, which explains much of the 3.7x drop in user CPU time; sys time rose from 24s to 1m25s. The README states no core count, CPU model, zip version or compression level, shows no compression ratio or archive size, and reports one run. It has no comparison with pigz, zstd, lz4, brotli or xz. The code is Go, not C++.

notes: Numbers verified on the README. License Apache-2.0, 123 stars, 6 forks, 148 commits, last commit 2023-12-10 (stale), not a fork, all confirmed. The DEFLATE engine is klauspost/compress, which is worth tagging for enrichment.
